items: Anti-NMDA encephalitis involves autoantibodies targeting the GluN1/NR1 subunit of the NMDA receptor (Dulcan p.370, StahlNeuro p.101)
Loss of NMDA receptor activation on cortical GABAergic interneurons causes pyramidal neuron disinhibition and mesolimbic dopamine surge (StahlNeuro p.105-108, p.110)
NPSLE involves microvascular vasculopathy, Anti-ribosomal P antibodies, Anti-NR2 antibodies, and cytokine-mediated BBB disruption (DSM p.132, p.730, Dulcan p.397)
PANDAS/PANS pathology targets the Caudate nucleus and Putamen within the Basal Ganglia, disrupting CSTC loops (Dulcan p.367, DSM p.292, StahlNeuro p.538-540)
key_numbers: 4 subunits - tetrameric NMDA receptor ion channel complex (StahlNeuro p.101)
2 striatal structures - Caudate and Putamen affected by anti-basal ganglia antibodies (Dulcan p.367)

items: Anti-NMDA encephalitis progresses from psychiatric prodrome to seizures, orofacial dyskinesia, autonomic instability, central hypoventilation, and coma (DSM p.132, Dulcan p.96, p.398)
NPSLE presents with Lupus psychosis, major depression, delirium, personality changes, and cognitive decline known as Lupus Fog (DSM p.132, p.730, Dulcan p.397)
PANDAS is defined by prepubertal abrupt overnight onset of OCD/tics with a sawtooth episodic course linked to GABHS infection (Dulcan p.368)
PANS requires abrupt onset of OCD or restricted food intake (ARFID-like) plus at least 2 of 7 accompanying symptom domains (Dulcan p.371, DSM p.292)
key_numbers: 3 to 12 years - prepubertal onset age range for PANDAS criteria (Dulcan p.368)
24 to 48 hours - timeframe to peak symptom severity in abrupt PANDAS/PANS onset (Dulcan p.368)
2 of 7 categories - minimum required accompanying symptom domains for PANS diagnosis (Dulcan p.371)
50% - prevalence of ovarian teratoma in post-pubertal females with Anti-NMDA encephalitis (DSM p.132, Dulcan p.96)

items: Anti-NMDA encephalitis mimics First-Episode Psychosis, Childhood-Onset Schizophrenia, Psychotic Mania, and Catatonia (DSM p.132, p.137, Dulcan p.397-398)
Steroid-Induced Psychosis develops 1-2 weeks post high-dose Prednisone (>40-60 mg/d) with normal complement C3/C4 levels, unlike primary NPSLE flares (DSM p.121, p.142, Dulcan p.235, p.397)
PANDAS/PANS presents with explosive onset and multisystem symptoms (dysgraphia, enuresis) contrasting with gradual primary pediatric OCD (Dulcan p.365, p.368, p.371)
DSM-5-TR classifies PANDAS/PANS under Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorder Due to Another Medical Condition (DSM p.292, p.959)
key_numbers: 1 to 2 weeks - onset window for steroid-induced psychosis following high-dose corticosteroid therapy (DSM p.142)
>40-60 mg/day - prednisone threshold dose associated with steroid psychosis (DSM p.142)

items: CSF anti-GluN1 (NR1) IgG antibody detection is the gold standard diagnostic test for Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis (Dulcan p.96)
EEG in Anti-NMDA encephalitis shows generalized slowing and the specific Extreme Delta Brush (EDB) pattern (Dulcan p.96)
Pelvic Ultrasound/MRI is mandatory to screen for Ovarian Teratoma in females with Anti-NMDA encephalitis (DSM p.132, Dulcan p.96)
NPSLE workup requires ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-ribosomal P, antiphospholipid antibodies, C3/C4 complement levels, and brain MRI (DSM p.730, Dulcan p.397)
PANDAS workup requires throat culture, rapid strep test, and paired ASO/Anti-DNase B titers taken 3-6 weeks apart (Dulcan p.376)
key_numbers: 30% - prevalence of Extreme Delta Brush (EDB) pattern on EEG in Anti-NMDA encephalitis (Dulcan p.96)
50% - proportion of Anti-NMDA encephalitis cases with initial normal brain MRI (Dulcan p.96)
3 to 6 weeks - mandatory interval between paired streptococcal serology samples (Dulcan p.376)
2-fold - required titer increase in paired ASO/Anti-DNase B serology for diagnosis (Dulcan p.376)

first_line: Anti-NMDA: IV Methylprednisolone pulse (30 mg/kg/d), IVIG (2 g/kg), Plasmapheresis (PLEX), and surgical resection of teratoma (Dulcan p.96)
NPSLE: IV Methylprednisolone pulse, Cyclophosphamide, and anticoagulation if antiphospholipid antibodies positive (Dulcan p.397)
PANDAS/PANS: CBT with Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) for OCD, and standard antibiotics (Penicillin/Amoxicillin) for active GABHS (Dulcan p.383)
second_line: Anti-NMDA: Rituximab (375 mg/m² weekly x 4) and Cyclophosphamide for refractory cases after 10-14 days (Dulcan p.96)
key_side_effects: Extreme Neuroleptic Sensitivity in Anti-NMDA encephalitis causing severe EPS, akathisia, and Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) (DSM p.810-811, Dulcan p.398)
Treatment-Emergent Activation Syndrome (TEAS) and akathisia from SSRIs in PANDAS/PANS requiring low starting doses (Dulcan p.150, StahlKids p.311, p.441)
treatment.monitoring: Monitor CPK, autonomic stability, and temperature when using low-dose atypical antipsychotics; monitor paired ASO titers at 3-6 week intervals; monitor renal and hepatic function in NPSLE (Dulcan p.376, p.680, DSM p.810-811)

high_yield: CSF anti-GluN1 IgG antibody testing is the gold standard diagnostic test for Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis with higher sensitivity than serum testing (Dulcan p.96)
High-dose corticosteroids (Prednisone >40-60 mg/d) can induce psychosis within 1-2 weeks; differentiate from primary NPSLE flare by normal C3/C4 complement levels (DSM p.142, Dulcan p.235)
Extreme Neuroleptic Sensitivity in Anti-NMDA encephalitis markedly increases NMS risk; high-dose Lorazepam is preferred for catatonia and agitation (DSM p.810, Dulcan p.398)
PANDAS criteria require prepubertal onset (ages 3-12), abrupt overnight OCD/tics, sawtooth course, paired streptococcal serology proof, and adventitious movements (Dulcan p.368)

A randomized sham-controlled trial by NIMH showed IVIG failed to demonstrate superiority over placebo for PANDAS; IVIG and chronic antibiotic prophylaxis are not recommended for routine use (Dulcan p.383, p.388)
